newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end weak following U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end weak following U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished slightly lower Tuesday on profit-taking, and in line with an early retreat on U.S. markets following the release of U.S. inflation data in line with expectations, dealers said.
"Prices were slightly depressed by profit-taking and took their cue from the U.S. markets' moves," said one dealer.

With the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond off 10/32 at a yield of 6.72 percent, despite tame U.S. consumer inflation for May of 0.1 percent and an industrial output rise of 0.4 percent, Argentine bonds dipped 0.25 percent on average with heavier profit-taking expected to emerge soon.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was unchanged by the close at 94-2/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 was down $0.01 at 121.11.
"These latest U.S. economic indicators are evidence of a bit of a slowdown in their economy, which gives institutional investors a breather," commented one Argentine bond trader.
